# Spacer

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:spacer` · Kerf UI · component · Structure

A decorative, non-shrinking fixed gap or flexible main-axis spacer with typed physical width and height.

## When to use

Express an intentional empty dimension or consume remaining flex space without application-owned spacer markup or raw CSS lengths.

- Reserve a fixed empty width or height from the UI spacing scale inside a layout.
- Push siblings to opposite ends of a Row or other flex container by passing flex.
- Use a typed CssLength when the finite spacing scale cannot express the required dimension.

**Not when:**

- Do not use Spacer for ordinary rhythm between siblings; prefer Row.gap or List.gap so the parent owns repeated spacing.
- Do not use Spacer to compensate for component-owned padding, margin, alignment, or responsive layout defects.
- Do not pass raw CSS strings to width or height.

**Alternatives:**

- [Row](./row.md) (parent-spacing-alternative) — Use Row.gap when every horizontal sibling needs the same repeated separation.
- [List](./list.md) (parent-spacing-alternative) — Use List.gap when every vertical sibling needs the same repeated separation.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/spacer` — exports `Spacer`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/spacer` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/spacer.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css.

## Props

Exact prop names and types: [`@kerfjs/ui/spacer`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuispacer) in `public-api-signatures-v1.md`. Do not infer props from examples.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- fixed named width and/or height
- fixed typed CssLength width and/or height
- flexible main-axis space

**CSS-value props** (typed builders from `@kerfjs/ui/css-values`; raw CSS strings are rejected):

- `width`: length grammar; raw values: forbid; shorthands `none`, `2xs`, `xs`, `m`, `l`; exceptional (justify) `s`, `xl`; helpers `px`, `rem`, `em`, `pct`, `space`, `lengthVar`, `calc` — e.g. `width="m"`
- `height`: length grammar; raw values: forbid; shorthands `none`, `2xs`, `xs`, `m`, `l`; exceptional (justify) `s`, `xl`; helpers `px`, `rem`, `em`, `pct`, `space`, `lengthVar`, `calc` — e.g. `height="xs"`

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** whether the empty space carries structural meaning; the named or typed dimensions; whether the spacer fills the flex main axis.

No wiring helper.

## Geometry

Margin: none · border: none · padding: none (layout role: structure). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

- A fixed Spacer does not shrink. flex changes its flex shorthand from 0 0 auto to 1 1 auto; width and height remain physical dimensions.

## Accessibility

- Spacer is always decorative and hidden from the accessibility tree.
- Spacer must not contain content or become an interaction target.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-spacer`.

Never put `kui-spacer` on an element you write; render `Spacer` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
